_emulation_only_rationale: Declares NO export_lane and is not shippable. It exists so Tessera's continuous rate axis can be ALLOCATED against gates that actually fire: an exact target_platform, so the E2M1 route's SM100 floor and the E4M3 route's SM89 floor are real comparisons against the GB10 the anchors were measured on, and an explicit tensor_parallel block, so shard legality is decided on the shape a rank will hold rather than on the whole tensor. It makes NO serving claim, and since 2026-09-02 the reason is the PIN rather than the table: Tessera's own packaged `runtime_contract.json` (schema tessera.runtime-contract.v1, read by tessera_render._pinned_serving_table) DOES publish TESSERA_E2M1_K2 and TESSERA_E4M3_K1 and carries device-qualified native cells for both receipted rungs, but no reviewed Tessera release tag exists, so require_exact_tessera_runtime_release refuses the pin and every rung resolves route_status `unattested` (tessera_menu.route_admission) and export fails closed. This sentence named the pinned GRIDBOOK release until 2026-09-02; Gridbook withdrew its Tessera lane that day (archive/gridbook_lane_2026-09-02/) and its pin stopped governing Tessera admission, so citing it here was a claim about a runtime that no longer answers. A Tessera rung selected under this profile is a REPORT about where the allocator would spend bytes, not an artifact.
description: RESEARCH-ONLY allocation profile for Tessera's three serialisable families (E2M1 K1, E2M1 K2, E4M3 K1) on GB10 (Blackwell sm_121), at the continuous 1/256-bpp rate axis. It admits the family set plus the scalar terminals an honest mixed menu needs, so a DP can rank a Tessera rung against NVFP4/FP8/BF16 in one currency.
_no_format_rules_rationale: Deliberately declares NO format_rules, exactly like the generic `research` profile and its trellis twin. Naming the ~3000 addressable rungs in an allow list would assert they are format_registry rows, and they are not: a rung's FormatSpec is synthesized on demand from its name (format_registry.get_format's Tessera fallback), because freezing a continuous rate axis into REGISTRY turns it into a menu someone has to maintain. The menu here is bounded on the Tessera side by tessera_menu.expand_tessera_menu -- family buildability, wire serialisability, shape legality, the TP shard, W(n<=A) and the route admission -- and on the scalar side by FORMATS plus check_format_applicability.

tensor_parallel._world_size_rationale: 1 is the honest default and also the pinned runtime's own ceiling for both Tessera families: the tensor_parallel table in Tessera's packaged runtime_contract.json (axis vllm_tensor_parallel_world_size, semantics closed_world) pins TESSERA_E2M1_K2 and TESSERA_E4M3_K1 at max_world_size 1. It cited gridbook_runtime_contract.0.9.1.json's TCQ_E2M1_R256/TCQ_E4M3_R256 rows until 2026-09-02: same conclusion, but read off a contract that left the tree with the Gridbook lane (archive/gridbook_lane_2026-09-02/), which is a derivation a reader cannot check. Raising it here without a contract that raises it there would allocate for a shard the runtime says it cannot serve. The rules below are declared at world_size 1 so the vocabulary is reviewed before the degree is, and so raising the degree is a one-token change rather than a new mapping.
tensor_parallel._rules_rationale: ENUMERATED, not inferred. `fused implies column-parallel` is wrong for units PrismaQuant already allocates -- MLA's q_a_proj and kv_a_proj_with_mqa are replicated, a router gate is replicated, and Qwen3.5's fused DeltaNet in_proj_qkvz is not head-sharded -- so the mapping is a declaration and an unmatched qname resolves to `none`, which makes the gate a no-op rather than a guess. Packed experts are `none` by construction in check_shape: expert parallelism cuts the stack and leaves each expert's 2-D unit whole.
